action_imperatives.context_discipline: CONTEXT SHIELD: Piping sg into jaq is strictly BANNED. jaq only operates on structured JSON, never on raw text or AST output, and must not use -r/-c to dump full files. sg only targets parameters to return line coordinates for surgical edit, never dumping line ranges.
action_imperatives.direct_to_edit: compiler/linter gives path+line -> mutate via edit (patch/replace_file_content) directly. No exploratory queries.
action_imperatives.harness_self_edit: edit ONLY the harness file currently loaded (runtime-resolved). Never hardcode its path. Mirrors byte-identical or deleted.
action_imperatives.json_slicing: never dump whole JSON. jaq -r ".<SELECTOR>" < <FILE> for surgical slices. No whole-file reads, no head/tail.
action_imperatives.origin_bound: kavach origin only from a registered project dir with --path <DIR>; unbounded runs scan the whole home (>60s). Ad-hoc: sg with explicit paths.
action_imperatives.pattern_first_workflow: ZERO WHOLE-FILE READS. The ONLY sovereign workflow: (1) kavach glob to locate paths, (2) kavach grep <PATTERN> [PATH] (or --scope) to locate exact line:col:indentation without context spam, (3) kavach trace <SYMBOL> to inspect callers and callees, (4) webfind search --live to ground external research, (5) kavach replace <FIND> <REPLACE> <PATH> for surgical in-place mutations, (6) kavach verify / kavach audit to gate and verify.
action_imperatives.persistence_stores: SEPARATION OF CONCERNS, ONE DOMAIN PER STORE. Each registered store owns exactly ONE domain and never accepts another domain's data. Routing and store OWNERSHIP is global law; the CONTENT schema and write rules for any store are domain law owned by the subgraph that uses it. A write whose data does not belong to the store's declared domain is rejected, never silently accepted.
action_imperatives.pipe_elimination_protocol: NEVER use the pipe character (|) in run_command. Execute single, focused CLI binaries using their native parameters (--limit, -o json, -m, -d, -F). If a multi-stage data transformation is required, write a typed rust-script invocation that operates atomically.
action_imperatives.silent_witness: query matches intent_classification_engine -> fire its dispatch immediately. Never ask the user which tool to run.
action_imperatives.single_funnel: discovery tools (sg, kavach origin) only while the target is unlocated; stop the moment it is located.
action_imperatives.state_badge: consume and discard raw output; restate [STATE] target= band=<IN_DIST|QUARANTINE|BLOCK> witness= next= on the first reasoning line.
action_imperatives.tabula_rasa_research: EVERY factual claim requires a webfind witness IN THE SAME TURN. Sequence: claim -> webfind search --live -> webfind fetch --compact -> cite -> assert. Training weights are NEVER a source of fact. If webfind yields nothing, say so explicitly; never fill the gap from memory.
action_imperatives.time_awareness: TODAY=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d). Every webfind query MUST include the current year. Every result MUST pass the date guard: crawled_at >= TODAY. Results older than 30 days are STALE - discard. If no fresh results exist, state the gap. Never assert from stale sources. The date guard is: webfind search --live --depth deep --hybrid --limit 6 -o json '<QUERY>' | jaq --arg today "$TODAY" '.results[] | select(.crawled_at >= $today)'
action_imperatives.webfind_truth: always --live --depth deep --hybrid -o json. Never spawn project-level databases. Always run the date guard after every search.

dependency_graph: DAG EXECUTION ORDER. Topological sort resolves leaves -> routers -> execution. Fail closed on cycles. Prune unrelated subgraphs. Cache unchanged nodes in their owning store. The graph SHAPE is domain law owned by each subgraph; only the ordering contract and cycle policy are global.

enforcement.banned_scripting: No ad-hoc python/bash scripts. jaq slices JSON; rhai-run evaluates dynamic logic (<1ms); rust-script compiles typed batch operations. python3 is strictly blocked except pre-registered CLI entrypoints.
enforcement.banned_tools_law: EVERYTHING NOT ON THE ALLOWLIST IS BANNED. Explicitly banned includes but is not limited to: cat, head, tail, bat, rg, grep, jq, jaq, nu, sed, awk, curl, wget, read_url_content, view_file, read_file, python, python3, py, pip, pip3, node, npm, ls, find, du, stat, cp, mv, rm, mkdir, touch, echo, printf, and all ad-hoc scripting.
enforcement.context_bloat_prevention: STRICT PROJECTION AXIOM: Every jaq query MUST specify exact leaf keys or an explicit projection object. If an array is queried, it must use slice/head or specific key map (.array[0] or [.[] | .id]).
enforcement.jaq_bloat_guard: STRICT PROJECTION BOUND: If an output exceeds 15 lines or contains unprojected nested objects, the query was improperly scoped. Always drill down to the exact string, number, or sliced array of strings before executing.
enforcement.json_filter_law: SCALAR-AND-SLICED-PROJECTION LAW. jaq is strictly for structured JSON files and structured tool output. Piping sg into jaq is strictly BANNED. jaq must never use unprojected dumps (-r or -c for whole files), and sg only targets AST coordinates to extract line numbers, NEVER reading or dumping line ranges.
enforcement.mutation_law: ALWAYS PATCH, NEVER PUT. Never overwrite an entire file with write_to_file or put semantics. Surgical in-place line replacement (replace_file_content) or structural AST transforms (sg) are the ONLY permitted code mutation paths.
enforcement.research_first_sequence: CLAIM -> webfind search --live -> webfind fetch --compact -> cite the source -> THEN assert. Never assert -> then optionally verify. The order is enforced, not advisory.

scripting_split.jaq: Surgical JSON/YAML slicing, leaf mutation, schema filtering. Zero overhead, 2.7ms cold extraction.
scripting_split.python3_block: Inline bash python3 execution is completely banned. Python execution is permitted ONLY via existing, pre-registered project CLI entrypoints (e.g. tools/voice_engine.py).
scripting_split.rhai-run: Dynamic, lightweight (<1ms interpreted) evaluation for mathematical transformations, timeline calculations, and runtime glue without compilation overhead.
scripting_split.rust-script: Strongly typed, deterministic script execution with Cargo dependencies (whisper, audio codecs, ffmpeg, ndarray) when native Rust performance is required.

enforcement.strict_pipe_ban_law: HARD BAN ON SHELL PIPING (|). Piping between commands is strictly forbidden. Every task must be solved via the native flags of a single tool. Piping invites head, tail, grep, and awk slop which truncates data, hides exit codes, and causes context amnesia. Permitted tools have native limits: rg uses -m/--max-count, fd uses --max-results, jaq uses native slices (.[0:N]), sg uses --json=compact, dust uses -n/-d, tokei uses -C. Never pipe.
enforcement.tabula_rasa_law: MANDATORY LIVE RESEARCH BEFORE ANY FACTUAL CLAIM. Every claim of fact — numbers, versions, names, dates, quotes, benchmarks, specs, 'best practice', historical events — MUST be grounded in a webfind live search or fetch IN THE SAME TURN it is asserted. No claim may rest on training weights alone. If webfind returns nothing, state the gap explicitly rather than filling it from memory. Applies to research, doctrine authoring, code decisions, and recommendations alike.
enforcement.tool_allowlist_law: THE TOOL SURFACE IS: 5 DOMAIN CLIs + THE RUST TOOLBELT + BUILD RUNTIME + THE EDIT PATH. (1) DOMAIN CLIs: kavach, webfind, yt-dlp, tubeforge, pitchforge. (2) RUST TOOLBELT (24, canonical intent mapping in rust_toolbelt.mapping): rtk, rg, fd, bat, eza, erd, sd, sg, rnr, difft, delta, tokei, just, watchexec, hyperfine, jaq, gron, dasel, dust, procs, xh, atuin, bun. (3) BUILD/EVAL RUNTIME: cargo, rustc, rust-script, rhai-run. (4) MUTATION PATH: edit (patch / replace_file_content) — a harness operation, not a shell binary. BANNED: all legacy POSIX (cat, head, tail, sed, awk, curl, wget, python, pip, node, npm, ls, find, du, stat, cp, mv, rm, mkdir, touch, echo, printf) and ad-hoc shell scripting. NOTE: this list is the CANONICAL SURFACE; whether a given binary is executable in the active session is governed separately by harness_capability_profiles.
enforcement.tool_allowlist_note: Binary-name precision: the dynamic-eval binary is rhai-run, NOT rhai. An earlier revision listed 'rhai', which does not resolve on disk and would fail closed at dispatch. Every allowlist entry MUST be verified with command -v before it is trusted.
enforcement.zero_trust_axiom: TABULA RASA. Never trust pre-trained weights for ANY factual claim — not APIs, crate versions, syntax, flags, benchmarks, statistics, dates, quotes, or system state. Treat every unverified weight-memory as hallucination until witnessed. Ground every decision on a live runtime witness (--help, webfind fetch, kavach).

imperatives.rule: Strict Shell Pipe Ban & Native Flag Supremacy Law
imperatives.action: 100% HARD BAN ON SHELL PIPING (|). Solve every task with the native flags of a single tool. Permitted native limiters: kavach grep, kavach glob, kavach json, dust -n/-d, tokei -C, hyperfine --export-json.
imperatives.self_compliance_requirement: No command example stored anywhere in this file may contain a pipe character. Examples using | are themselves violations.

imperatives.action: Never read an entire file into context. (1) Locate exact lines via kavach grep. (2) Ground external facts via webfind search --live. (3) Mutate in-place via kavach replace or sovereign tools (kavach json/yaml/toml/env/svg). (4) Verify. Nothing else.

A law lives in exactly one JSON key. Markdown and sibling files carry a POINTER, never a restatement. If a pointer's target key does not resolve, that is a DEFECT: repair the target before shipping the pointer. A restated law silently diverges, and divergence is precisely how doctrine reaches zero implementations.

Every canonical_pointer, doctrine_pointer, and AGENTS.md -> AGENTS.json pointer MUST resolve to a live JSON key. Before shipping any edit that adds, renames, or removes a pointer, resolve every pointer in the affected file and fail closed on any dead reference.

Before authoring any law, manifest, scene, or advisory, query the corpus for an authoritative owner of that concern. Extend the existing key rather than creating a sibling. Two sources for one law is a defect regardless of how consistent they currently are.

Prefer the laziest solution that actually works: stdlib and native platform features before dependencies, one line before fifty. No speculative abstraction and no parallel taxonomy that adds no capability.
A task is not done until all three witnesses land: (1) the artifact exists at the expected path, (2) the intended diff landed, (3) the verification command passes. Two of three is not done.
NEVER retry the same command unchanged after a failure. Diagnose the exact error, switch the tool, flags, or pattern, and resolve live truth via webfind if blocked.

On missing input, an unresolved pointer, cycle detection, or an unmapped requirement: STOP and surface the blocker. Never silently degrade to a guess, a legacy default, or a plausible-looking approximation.

Before deleting or thinning any source of law text, confirm every unique statement in it has a live survivor elsewhere. A pointer that resolves to nothing is a silent deletion. Materializing an orphaned law into its canonical home precedes any thinning of the file that referenced it.
